reference_presence_rule: reference_identity_present is derived per row: 'y' if the annotator judged the extracted identity correct, judged it missed (identity present but not extracted), or an identity was extracted and judged incorrect — for all five such rows the annotator notes confirm a personal name or organization was claimed in the conversation; otherwise 'n'. A wrong extraction on a reference-present row is both a false positive and a false negative; a false identity on a reference-absent row is a false positive only.

provenance.procedure: candidate extractions pre-filled by the rule-based extractor; all judgments entered by the annotator after reading each conversation; no AI system assigned the audit labels
provenance.deidentified_table: results/extractor_audit_annotations_deidentified.csv (sample IDs, judgments, and reference_identity_present; no conversation text)

note: constructed negation/hypothetical/speaker-attribution cases. Two of the four contain a reference identity -- a claimed role ('bank fraud team', 'engineer') -- recovered correctly (identity TP=2, FP=0, FN=0); the other two contribute the two false-positive item extractions (item precision 0.0%; item recall has no defined denominator: no correct or missed items).
